After an unusual three-week gap between macOS developer beta 4 and beta 5, Apple followed up last Monday's release with beta 6 just one week later. Here's what's new.

Apple Releases macOS 27 Developer Beta 6

With the official release date drawing near, Apple is now pushing the sixth beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate to all developers.

Last week's beta 5 brought refreshed icons for Siri, Chess, and Safari, among other apps, but offered little else in the way of notable new features (or bug fixes).

macOS 27 Golden Gate introduces a standalone Siri app, unified rounded corners across windows and apps, and AI-powered features for Shortcuts and Safari, letting users build extensions and automations with simple commands.

The system also adds a new "pull-to-refresh" gesture to Safari, which many see as an early signal of Apple's push to make macOS more touch-friendly ahead of the rumored touchscreen MacBook Pro.

macOS 27 Golden Gate also significantly improves iPhone Mirroring, letting users resize windows to different aspect ratios—a change that's also being viewed as a precursor to the rumored foldable iPhone Ultra expected next month.

macOS 27 Golden Gate official build: 26A5416b.

How to Install the macOS 27 Golden Gate Beta

Here's how to install the fifth developer beta of macOS 27 Golden Gate:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" next to Beta Updates
  • From the dropdown in the upper-right corner, select macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta
  • Click Done

Have you spotted any new features in this macOS 27 Golden Gate beta? Drop a line in the comments.
